fit: inhaled marjoram and short EEG segments in young men
assessment: Theta and right-temporal beta findings vary by baseline sleep group. No attention task or culinary arm.

fit: marjoram oil inhalation and neurofeedback device divergence
assessment: Thirteen exposed and thirteen unexposed. Global repeated result p=.091 with favorable selected-session contrasts. No participant attention test.

fit: marjoram nasal filter, neurofeedback and bruxism
assessment: No clear difference in perceived stress between exposed and unexposed trained patients. Device and saliva measures do not give clinical attention change.

fit: injected marjoram leaf extract and mouse memory tasks
assessment: Novel object ratio and Y-maze alternation favored pretreatment versus LPS. Different cognitive tasks, injection and non-Parkinson model leave clinical attention unresolved.

fit: oral bay leaf decoction and rat exploration or immobility
assessment: Higher bay concentration increased swim immobility from control mean 43.87 to 114.6 seconds despite favorable abstract wording. Low concentration outcome and open-field measures differ. No apathy task.

fit: rosemary in mixed throat spray and composite symptom response
assessment: Twenty-minute response 19/26 vs 14/34, p=.019. Three-day comparison p=.42. The published control heading conflicts with Methods and percentages. No separate hoarseness or voice loudness estimate.

fit: related Zanthoxylum oil inhalation with exercise and postural sway
assessment: The eyes-closed velocity comparison favored intervention at four weeks and follow-up. Dynamic reach and fear of falling had inconclusive interactions. Related species and inhalation do not identify ground Sichuan pepper.

fit: isolated beta caryophyllene in a mouse pole test
assessment: Oral pretreatment reduced pole time compared with the toxin model. The isolated constituent, exact timing and clinical outcome differ from the frozen claim.

fit: injected dill leaf and other extracts in rodent movement tests
assessment: Higher leaf and fruit extracts reduced simple locomotion. This neither assesses hand dexterity nor identifies an effect from eating fresh dill weed.

fit: reduced spontaneous locomotion after injected dill extracts
assessment: Dose-dependent locomotor changes are described as sedative, with no direct sleep or insomnia assessment. Part and preparation differ.

fit: allspice oil and eugenol toxicity observations in an arthritis model
assessment: The original report describes mucosal irritation, breathing difficulty and sedation. It gives no acoustic or listener-rated speech endpoint.

fit: ketogenic diet and Parkinson patient-reported voice handicap
assessment: Reported VHI-10 means favor the ketogenic group after three months. The intervention does not assign a named coconut oil and the voice handicap instrument does not measure intelligibility.

fit: safflower oil capsules and bowel tolerability
assessment: Some volunteer participants reported bloating. No tally of constipation, bowel rate or stool consistency during the active period. The comparison did not establish oil refining.

fit: safflower-containing comparator and registered bowel diaries
assessment: Protocol measures stool frequency and consistency in a synbiotic comparison. High-oleic safflower is one placebo ingredient. No posted outcomes.

fit: kefir after exercise and patient-reported fatigue in cancer survivors
assessment: The 24-person article abstract reports 39.3% fatigue improvement. The likely related 19-person dissertation reports an interaction p=.002. Product flavor, full article contrast and Parkinson treatment remain unverified.

fit: kefir, milk and water and acute postexercise fatigue
assessment: Postexercise fatigue improved with kefir and water before retesting. The author abstract does not show a clear kefir superiority estimate.

fit: kefir during cancer treatment and aggregate physical symptoms
assessment: The fourth-cycle physical symptom outcome favors the kefir arm. Tiredness is one physical item and is not given separately. Product flavor and contribution of extra contact remain unclear.

fit: commercial kefir in myeloma and planned patient fatigue measures
assessment: Official protocol names fatigue. No primary result or exact product grade was verified.

fit: kefir powder and planned fatigue visual analog rating
assessment: Physical fatigue is secondary in the 75-person powder protocol. Results are unpublished in the official record.

fit: commercial kefir and registered PROMIS Global Health
assessment: A planned fatigue item in a broader outcome supplies no result. Observational protocol without a parallel untreated comparison group.
